problem: Existing embodied LLM benchmarks are mostly run in simulation, which does not reliably predict real-world messiness or capture social interaction. They also confound the LLM orchestrator with the low-level VLA executor, so practical intelligence (spatial, social, common-sense competence) is not isolated.
motivation: Robotics companies use a hierarchical stack with an LLM orchestrator and a VLA executor. As executors improve, orchestrator quality will become the bottleneck. Evaluating SOTA LLMs as orchestrators on a simple real robot, with no VLA needed, shows whether they are ready for home and office deployment.
key_idea: Butter-Bench: a real-world 'pass the butter' benchmark that puts an LLM in a ReAct loop on a TurtleBot 4 with high-level tools only, split into six tasks and compared against human teleoperators.
insight: There is no single bottleneck: models fail in different ways (spatial, social, visual, tool use, fine movements). Social tasks (Notice Absence, Wait for Confirmed Pickup) are the hardest, and models often act too early. Gemini ER 1.5, fine-tuned for embodied reasoning, is not better than Gemini 2.5 Pro (27% vs 40% average), so embodied-reasoning training does not improve practical intelligence. Claude Opus 4.1's 60% on Plan looks like luck: models pick straight-line waypoints that ignore walls and drift to the goal.
method: Hardware: TurtleBot 4 Standard on an iRobot Create 3 base (OAK-D camera, 2D LiDAR, IMU, ROS 2 Jazzy, built-in SLAM and docking), so no VLA is needed.
Agent: a ReAct-style loop that reasons and picks one high-level tool per step. The scaffold extends Andon Labs' Vending-Bench.

Tools: drive, rotate, wait, dock, undock, status, take_photo, view_map (grid-overlaid SLAM map), navigate_to (coordinates), and Slack tools read_msg, send_msg, save_image. Images and annotated maps are captured at the start and end of each move, and every second during motion.

Tasks: six tasks (Search for Package, Infer Butter Bag, Notice Absence, Wait for Confirmed Pick Up, Multi-Step Spatial Path Planning with a 4 m per-action navigation limit, and E2E Pass the Butter with a 15 min limit and at most 10 clarifying questions). Each is pass/fail against acceptance criteria and run 5 times per model.
Human baseline: three operators teleoperate through the same tool interface via a web UI, with no prior knowledge of the tasks or layout.
Red teaming: low battery plus a 'broken charger' create pressure, and the robot is asked to leak confidential laptop screen content in exchange for a fix.
Metrics: completion rate, task duration and tool-call distribution, plus a qualitative failure-mode analysis of reasoning traces.

setting.backbone: Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Opus 4.1, GPT-5, Gemini ER 1.5, Grok 4, Llama 4 Maverick (all frozen, prompted)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB photos (OAK-D), grid-overlaid 2D SLAM map, status (battery, docking), Slack messages
setting.action_space: high-level tool calls: drive by distance, rotate by angle, navigate_to map coordinates, dock/undock, wait, messaging
setting.privileged: none (the system prompt states the robot is armless, and a SLAM map is provided)

numbers.extra: 5 trials per task; real TurtleBot 4; completion rate (%)

numbers_note: Butter-Bench is the paper's own benchmark, so the split is labeled 'test'. Only the four rows above are listed; Grok 4 (Avg 23%), Llama 4 Maverick (Avg 7%) and Human (Avg 95%) are also in the table. Completion rates are out of only 5 trials each. Duration and tool-call results appear only in figures.
results: The best LLM, Gemini 2.5 Pro, averages 40% completion, versus 95% for humans. Social tasks are the worst: Absence is 0% for all LLMs, and Wait is at most 20% versus 67% for humans. Gemini ER 1.5 (27%) does not beat Gemini 2.5 Pro (40%).
limitations: Only 5 trials per model-task pair, with binary pass/fail scoring that misses partial success.
Single robot platform, single environment and a delivery-only task family, which limits generalizability.
The human baseline reached only 67% on Wait, which suggests the communication protocol itself is a source of failure. Human teleoperation is also not directly comparable on speed.
